_what: Ceilings that may only ever go DOWN. Raising one is allowed exactly once per deliberate decision, in its own commit, with the reason in the message.
_measured_at: 2026-09-18: 7454 -> 7496, deliberately and once. A quiet station was knocked at for as long as playback stood, which is right for a stream that dropped and wrong for one that has gone away. The widget cannot tell those apart, so the ladder got a budget instead of a diagnosis: three tries over about three and a half minutes, then it stops (issue #13). The lines went on four things. The ladder's arithmetic moved to RetryLogic.js and is called rather than inlined. The switch and the budget collapsed into one _mayKnock asked from every road that may refuse, because 2026.37 shipped with the switch read at one of two roads. The give-up now ENDS the standing order instead of only silencing the ladder — netResumeTimer resumes on that order alone, so an order outliving its ladder put a dead station on hours later, which was the original report and was still open with retries switched off. And the off-the-air message says which of the three things is about to happen instead of promising background retries a switched-off road was never going to make. Ceiling = wc -l package/contents/ui/main.qml
_how_to_remeasure: direct_exec:      grep -rhoE 'executable\.exec\(' package --include='*.qml' | wc -l   (then subtract the facade's own body — tests/test_ratchet.py does that part)
